messages:
Alice: heads-up — eval-alerts bumped a spike for the 'payments-json' eval after rolling out mix-quant autopick yesterday evening. hallucination rate up ~4.2% vs baseline :frowning_face:
Ben: saw it too from the dashboard. spike aligns with the 21:00 deploy that enabled the new kernel scheduler heuristics + per-layer mixed calibration.
Carlos: is this the one that switches kernels mid-request based on batch composition? can you paste the alert?
Alice: eval-alerts-bot: ALERT payments-json: metric=structured_failure_rate, baseline=0.6%, current=4.8%, p95-latency bump ~7ms.
Diana: quick hypothesis: scheduler is coalescing sequences with different pad lengths -> runtime chooses a different kernel variant that expects a different calibration table (per-kernel scaling mismatch). That could corrupt logits ordering for structured output and cause missing keys.
Ben: interesting — profiling from the canary VM shows several kernel switches at token 12 and 24 boundaries for some batches. kernel_choice log: `selected_kernel=fp8_mxv_12x64_v2 -> fallback=int8_dot_8x32`
Carlos: fallback path might be applying a different quant params table (we only calibrate per-model, not per-kernel-selection). if scales are incompatible we could get degenerate softmax and top-token drift.
Alice: repro steps I ran locally (small):
```
# run a mini-batch that previously failed
python run_repro.py --model redwood-3b-mix --batch-sizes 3,1,5 --seq-lens 128,16,256 --use-autopick
```
Output was truncated JSON for 2/10 seeds.
Diana: can you dump KV cache checksums after each layer? if coalescing shards are reusing offsets incorrectly that'll also corrupt outputs.
Ben: added a quick patch to runtime to log `kv_checksum` per-request and per-layer for failing traces. pushed to debug branch and re-ran repro. saw mismatch between checksum at replay vs live when kernel switched.
Carlos: which component handles batch coalescing? sched-batcher v2? It has the new heuristic that groups by earliest-deadline-first + pad-minimization. Maybe it's grouping sequences that should be separated to preserve per-request kernel binding.
Alice: agree. telemetry query I ran: `select count(*) from traces where kernel_switches > 0 and structured_failure = true` -> 312 hits in 24h mostly from high-mix customers and requests with long/short seq combos.
Diana: short-term mitigation: add a guard in the scheduler to avoid kernel_switch within a request (force single kernel variant per request) and disable the pad-merging optimization for mixed-quant rollout. low-risk and quick to revert.
Ben: also propose: extend calibration step to produce per-kernel calibration tables and embed kernel_id in the request metadata so fallback kernels pick compatible scales. longer-term.
Carlos: on the hallucination metric: is it actual semantic hallucination or structural (JSON keys missing/malformed)? Alice?
Alice: mostly structural: missing fields and truncated arrays. Behavioral hallucinations not as pronounced in these cases. correlates with `softmax_entropy` spikes in telemetry.
Diana: tasks: 1) immediate scheduler guard (Diana), 2) KV checksum alert + replay collection (Ben), 3) produce per-kernel calib artifacts roadmap (Carlos + ML), 4) run canary rollback policy for autopick (Alice).
Ben: I'll open a small PR for the scheduler guard, will include a feature flag `disable_intra_request_kernel_switch` and default it ON for rollout.
Carlos: ML action: we'll run targeted calibration runs for the top 3 kernel variants and produce per-layer scale tables. might need small changes to on-disk calib format to version by kernel-id.
Alice: created a minimal repro set in the eval harness (10 prompts) and pinned model+seed. Sharing link: https://internal.eval/repro/2333214321
Diana: for observability, add a new metric `kv_checksum_mismatch` and tag by kernel_switch_count and batch_coalesce_count. This will help quantify fix impact.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: branch=runtime/avoid-intra-kernel-switch, env=staging, owner=Ben
Ben: staging deploy done. initial test on flagged customer traffic in staging shows structured_failure_rate -> 0.9% (from 4.8%). still running more iterations.
Alice: nice. can we also surface kernel id in the console per-route so SRE can filter?
Carlos: UI change is small; I'll file a ticket.
Diana: long-term: scheduler should be kernel-aware; treat kernel-selection as part of placement constraints so batching doesn't mix incompatible kernel requirements. also consider calibration-aware fallback mapping so fallback kernels have transform functions to align scales.
Ben: note: watch latency — forcing single kernel per-request may increase effective latency for tiny requests if we can't coalesce them. but perf regressions might be acceptable short-term to fix correctness.
Alice: agreed. I'm voting for correctness-first. rolling guard to 100% for autopick rollback if we see customer impact >1% after 24h.
Carlos: will start per-kernel calibration runs tomorrow and push artifacts to model-catalog under `redwood-3b-mix/calib/v2/` 
Alice: update: eval-alerts-bot reports a drop: structured_failure_rate now 0.8% on staging within 45m.
Diana: good signal. leave this thread open for the next 24h and we'll move tasks to the sprint board. Thanks all. :tada:
